text:
amanda: Heads up — found a weird edgecase: when I rotate my API key in the Console while a long-lived CLI upload is running, the upload keeps using the old key for ~20–30s and then 403s out. Retry logic gives up fast. Repro steps below.

raj: ugh, thanks. can you paste the CLI output?

amanda: pasted below. it's short.
```
$ rw-cli upload --project oak --file model.tar
Uploading chunk 3/12
Error: 403 Forbidden: invalid api key
Retries exhausted
```

tess: quick q — does the CLI watch env vars or only read them at start? iirc it reads on startup.

amanda: it reads on startup. i tried `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=xxx && kill -HUP <pid>` thinking HUP might reload, but it didn't.

miguel: two things happening: (1) server-side key revocation is slightly eventual in some regions, (2) client treats 403 as fatal and doesn't attempt a refresh or ask the user for new creds. both small but annoying.

raj: agree. minimal fix: treat 403/401 on streaming uploads as a soft error -> attempt one token refresh/lookup (re-read env + ~/.config) then retry once. fallback to fatal after that.

amanda: that would solve 90% of my pain. also we should doc the env var precedence somewhere obvious: REDWOOD_API_KEY env > CLI cred file (~/.config/redwood/creds) > token-cache. saved me a lot of guessing.

ops-bot: incident created: RBW-2345 — CLI key rotation during long streams (low severity).

raj: i'll open a tiny PR to change retry behavior and add a test simulating server-side revocation + env switch. tagging @eng-runtime for server headers: can we return `Retry-After` or `X-Reauth-Required: 1` on immediate revocations so clients can react deterministically?

miguel: SGTM. also adding a small note in onboarding sample-app: "If you rotate keys while a long-running process is active, restart the process or use the CLI restart command." saves future confusion.

amanda: thanks all — i'll add the sample-app blurb and attach the CLI logs to the PR once raj opens it. :thumbsup:
